ui.name: Yumok 流木 Lee Dong-joo
ui.lead: A hydraulic engineer who spent his life calculating how water flows picked up a camera and photographed its surface. These are the 282 pictures he chose himself. Please take your time.

ui.filmText: 24 January 2019, Simpo Port, Gimje. Filmed by the photographer himself. Before it became a photograph, this is how the water he was watching moved.
ui.soundNote: The sound in this hall was recorded by his camera that day.
ui.logTitle: The days he went out for water light
ui.logSub: 2018 – 2022 · {n} days · dates and places as he wrote them on his folders

hallText.abstract: When ripples scatter the light, familiar things remain only as colour and line.
hallText.reflection: The surface shows the world upside down, and a little shaken.
hallText.pattern: The patterns that wind and water draw again and again.
hallText.landscape: The lakes and harbours, valleys and seas where he went to photograph water.

ui.river: Yumok (流木) means driftwood: wood carried along by water.
timeline: Graduates in civil engineering and begins to teach
Doctorate for research on tidal models
Professor of civil engineering, Kunsan National University
Gathers five years of water light by his own hand
finale: My father asked me to build a website where he could show his photographs.
I kept putting it off, saying I was busy.
This hall is what I could not make for him while he was alive,
built late by his son Seungheon, with regret and with longing.

site.He served for 46 years in the Department: He served for 46 years in the Department of Civil Engineering at Kunsan National University, including as professor, dedicating himself to nurturing the next generation of scholars, and was awarded the Order of Civil Merit with Yellow Stripes. After retirement, he pursued photography, creating works of profound philosophy and artistry centered on water and light.
site.His photographs capture the fleeting lan: His photographs capture the fleeting landscapes created by driftwood dancing in the harmony of light and water. We invite you to appreciate the works of the late Lee Dong-joo, who expressed the pure and transient beauty of nature through poetic and artistic photography, and hope they inspire you deeply.

He taught the flow of water as a hydraulic engineer for 46 years, and in his last years he photographed water and light. If someone asks about these pictures, please say his name.
